text:
ana: FYI I started the onb for nova_bridge -> llm-mistral-compat int4. initial small-batch eval shows negative ROUGE on Q&A style dataset: answers are shorter and drop named entities (person/place). suspiciously model seems to merge tokens around capitalized names.

chao: capitalized merging could be a tokenization casefold/normalization issue or vocab remap where some proper nouns map to subtoken combos differently. did the converter use --preserve-vocab?

ana: yes preserve-vocab used. roundtrip hash is equal to baseline, so token ids match on short samples. but longer context shows different segmentation near punctuation and capitals. could be our tokenizer's byte-level normalization versus model's original pretokenization.

chao: please run the tokenizer diff tool with --show-spans and paste an example of a name that drops. Also check embedding similarity for entity tokens pre- and post-conversion.

ana: example: 'Dr. Lucia Montoya' becomes ['Dr', '.', 'Luc', 'ia', ' Mont', 'oya'] vs baseline ['Dr', '.', 'Lucia', ' Montoya'] — so split occurs inside Lucia. embedding cos for 'Lucia' token area drops from 0.91 to 0.66 post-convert at generation time.

ci-bot: nightly-onboard/nova_mistral-int4 flagged rouge-drop > 0.7 on qa-suite (run https://ci.redwood.ai/runs/5101)

chao: two-pronged: 1) tokenizer normalization mismatch is primary suspect; add a forced pretokenizer step during conversion that runs the model's original tokenizer export (if available) to produce canonical token boundaries. 2) For quick mitigation, add a named-entity postprocessor that re-merges adjacent subtokens mapping to capitalized sequences (only in inference wrapper, as a stop-gap). We'll also add a corpus-level check for capitalized-splits to onboarding CI.

ana: added NER merge hack in the runtime wrapper and re-ran Q&A: ROUGE improves by +0.8 but we must keep it temporary. I'll open an issue to upstream tokenizer export support for the model archive.

chao: good. also record exact failing examples in onboarding artifacts to help later testcases. If tokenizer-export isn't available, we should add a conversion-time merge table heuristics derived from corpus frequency.

ana: logging examples in artifacts now. will follow up with PR for the NER merge flag in runtime. :memo:
